newsitem.title: JAPAN: China says Japan must take measures on islands.
newsitem.headline: China says Japan must take measures on islands.

text.p: China's Vice Foreign Minister Tang Jiaxuan said on Tuesday that Japan must take measures to defuse tensions over disputed islands in the East China Sea, a Japanese Foreign Ministry official said.

"The most important thing is for the Japanese side to take appropriate measures to resolve the issue," a Japanese official quoted Tang as telling Japanese Deputy Foreign Minister Shunji Yanai in Tokyo. Tang did not elaborate.

His remarks referred to a dispute over a group of tiny uninhabited islets, which Japan calls the Senkakus and China calls the Diaoyus, that flared up after Japanese ultra-nationalists erected a lighthouse earlier this year on one of the islands, which are also claimed by Taiwan.
The meeting of the two vice ministers was the first formal talks between senior diplomats of Japan and China since a brief meeting late last month in New York between their foreign ministers.

Senior Japanese Foreign Ministry officials have said the dispute over the islands and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's visit to a controversial war shrine in July have plunged Sino-Japanese relations to their worst state since ties were normalised in 1978.
Tang told Yanai that actions and remarks by Japanese politicians regarding Japan's actions in World War Two could have repercussions, the Japanese official said.

"The issue of historical perspective is central to bilateral ties, and words and actions (by Japanese leaders) could invite reactions from the Chinese people," the Japanese official quoted Tang as saying.
Last month, the dispute of the islands flared up anew after the death of a pro-China Hong Kong activist in a protest in the waters around them.
Japanese coastguard vessels have tried to keep Taiwanese and Hong Kong protesters from landing on the islands, but some have landed on them to wave flags in protest.
In the New York meeting, Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda promised not to ignore the issue of the lighthouse, although he did not promise concrete action.
